notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Two pages opened (Khorshidi dynasty, Hazaraspids). Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Dates: the infobox gives 1184-1597 (the lead prints '1597-1184'); the founder's start is '1174/1184'; the end is 1597 (infobox) or 1597-98 (Shahverdi killed by Shah Abbas).
Territory: Lorestan province (Little Lorestan, Khorramabad, Borujerd). The page also has two rulers (Falak al-Din Hasan and Izz al-Din Husayn, both d. 1293) who 'established control over all the lands between Hamadan and Shushtar, and between Isfahan and the Arab lands' (undated, not drawn), and Muhammad Sultan, governor of Fars, extending authority over all of Luristan and Khuzestan in 1395-96. The Hazaraspid dossier (Greater Lorestan) leaves the province to this one.
Status (suzerain-side events not recorded here): Abaqa Khan killed the sons of Badr al-Din Masud (Masud ruled to 1260; the killing is undated); in 1296 a ruler was killed near Khorramabad and 'the real authority was under the Mongols'; in 1383 Muzaffarid Shah Shoja visited Khorramabad with an army; Shah Husayn Abbasi was killed in 1466-67 or 1468-69 by Baharlu Turks on an expedition to Shahrizor (the page names no state); 'the Khorshidi dynasty remained an important player in the rivalry between the Safavids and the Ottomans'. Muhammadi's 1578-95 submission to Murad III is an Ottoman suzerainty over the new territories west of Iran.
Not settled: the dates of the Murad III territories (Badra, Jassan and Tursaq are not in the gazetteer and not drawn; Mandali is), the years of the two reaches above, the 1242 defeat of Husamuddin bin Khalil near Khorramabad (victor implied: Sulayman Shah Aywa), the wars with the Hazaraspids.
Gazetteer names used that it lacks: none (Badra, Jassan and Tursaq are not drawn).
